From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Defining acceptance criteria for our evaluation

Clara —

Attached is an initial MAP (MAP-Medspring-v1.xlsx) + a 1-page acceptance stoplight I put together. Key points up front so it’s easy to circulate: 

1) High-level success criteria (must be met for green):
   • Functional accuracy: >= 89% labeled-correct on the agreed prompt set (see tab "Eval Prompts").
   • Latency: p95 <= 450ms for single-request path at target concurrency (concurrency=8).
   • Stability: no more than 1 incident impacting >=10% of requests over 72 hours during the eval window.
   • Cost proxy: inference cost per 1k tokens within 20% of the initial estimate in the MAP.

2) Exit gates / stoplight (GO / REVIEW / NO-GO):
   • GO (green): all green criteria above + security checklist passed (SOC2 evidence on file).
   • REVIEW (amber): one soft metric misses threshold (e.g., cost or latency slightly over), requires mitigation plan and re-run.
   • NO-GO (red): functional accuracy <82% or repeated stability incidents.

3) Acceptance tests we’ll run (concrete):
   • Functional concordance: run 1,200 labeled prompts (seeded + customer edge cases) and report precision/recall. Pass if >=89%.
   • Robustness / edge-case sampling: 200 adversarial prompts, fail if >15% hallucination rate on critical fields.
   • Latency/Load: incremental load test up to 8 concurrent sustained workers for 24 hours; collect p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
   • Regression checks: compare outputs to baseline model (vX) on parity tasks; flag major deltas >5% on key metrics.

4) Timeline (two-week evaluation example):
   • Day 0: MAP sign-off & onboarding (API keys, sample data).
   • Days 1–3: integration + smoke tests (quick functional checks).
   • Days 4–9: full functional evaluation & load testing.
   • Days 10–12: remediation (if needed) and re-test.
   • Day 13–14: acceptance review + stakeholder sign-off.

Next steps: Soojin will share the technical runbook and the exact curl tests we’ll run. Marissa will add stakeholder sign-off owners and procurement touchpoints (HubSpot/DocuSign links). If this looks good, Clara, can you confirm the evaluation window you prefer (we proposed Feb 9–22) and the list of red-lines for your legal/procurement team?

I’ll also include the smoke-runbook PDF and sample load results from a recent pilot for reference.

Thanks — Mateo
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Adding the technical runbook and a few clarifying points — see attached smoke-runbook-v1.pdf. Highlights: 

- Smoke checklist (to run on Day 1): auth + token validation, sample inference on 20 canonical prompts, KV cache warmup test, and end-to-end logging verification.
- Load test plan: step-up schedule 1 -> 4 -> 8 workers, each step 2 hours, sustained 24h at 8 workers. Collect CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, p95 latency.
- Metrics to capture/ship: request_id, prompt_sha, model_variant, response_latency_ms, error_type, tokens_generated. We’ll export a CSV sample (attached: load-tests-results-20260206.csv).
- Acceptance threshold clarifications: p95 target is 450ms for the standard path; if Medspring wants a tighter SLA we can propose a Dedicated pool but that will change cost profile.

Technical ask for Clara: please confirm the canonical prompt set and a small seed of 30 private edge cases we should include in the 1,200 evaluation set (we can redact PII and run in the hosted tenant).

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
